answer: Each agent can post trades only after locking a scarce, slashable bond in a shared ledger; a kernel checks that one bond backs each active identity and records signed orders. When an agent defaults or double-spends, peers prove the conflicting messages and the bond is forfeited to affected traders. A sybil attacker can still create names, but each one needs separate capital tied up at risk, making fake identities costly rather than free; shale and ferrous are merely labels, not extra identities.
